verdict.line: You lose if you let her stack Riposte parries and farm Duelist procs for free; you win if you bait a bad Q (Lunge) or land Counter Strike first.

brief.thesis: This lane is decided by who dodges the other's hard CC first — OP.GG's own read confirms it: whoever lands Counter Strike (E) or Riposte (W) wins the fight. Jax vs Fiora sits at 48.5% over 2912 games, genuinely even, because both champions win by baiting the other's defensive cooldown and then all-inning the window after it's spent.

theirWindow.when: Riposte is up and she's full HP
theirWindow.what: She can parry your next auto to reflect magic damage and buff her AD — don't throw an auto into a clearly baited stance; wait it out or use Q (Leap Strike) to close distance from a weird angle instead.

yourWindow.when: Her W (Riposte) and both E (Burst of Speed) charges are down
yourWindow.what: This is your all-in window. Leap Strike in, pop W (Empower) on the strike, and immediately chain into E (Counter Strike) — the stun from Counter Strike is unconditional and doesn't care about her cooldowns, so this is where you force the fight.

start.why: 48.2% win rate over 1855 games and the majority pick — the extra sustain and AD let you contest her early Lunge trades instead of getting poked out.

boots.why: 73.2% pick rate at 47.7% win — the flat damage reduction on her auto-reset trade pattern (Lunge into autos) outweighs the MR from Mercury's Treads against a near-zero-magic-damage kit.

core.why: Spellblade procs off Leap Strike or Empower give you the burst to win an all-in the instant her Riposte is down.
The crit-on-first-hit and healing proc directly counters her Duelist sustain race once fights go long.

runes.keystoneWhy: 27.2% pick at 46.9% win — the stacking attack speed rewards exactly the extended auto-trade pattern you want once her Riposte parry is on cooldown, since you're not feeding it a single telegraphed auto.

summoners.why: 75.7% pick rate on Flash+Ignite at 48.6% win — Ignite's sustained burn cuts directly into her Duelist healing in all-ins, which matters more here than Teleport's scaling since this lane is decided by fights, not farm leads.

playing.title: Track her E charge state
playing.detail: Burst of Speed (E) gives attack speed and ramping move speed on landed hits; if she's already popped it and is chasing, don't try to kite — turn and Counter Strike to punish the chase.

playing.title: Never auto into standing Riposte
playing.detail: If she stops moving and squares up without initiating, that's the Riposte bait. Walk one auto's distance back or threaten with Leap Strike's range (700) instead of feeding the parry.

playing.title: All-in only when both her cooldowns are down
playing.detail: Riposte (W) and both Lunge (Q) charges spent is your green light — Leap Strike in, Empower (W) the strike, then land Counter Strike's stun before she can reset with Burst of Speed.

playing.title: Respect double-Lunge poke pre-6
playing.detail: Her Q can be thrown twice within a couple seconds at no mana cost — don't walk up for a last-hit right after she's used one charge, since the second is still live.

playing.title: Hold Counter Strike for her all-in, not yours
playing.detail: Counter Strike's stun is undodgeable and doesn't require baiting a cooldown like Riposte does — if she commits with Q into an auto string, your E stun wins the exchange outright.

playing.title: Play around Blade Waltz timer from level 6
playing.detail: Her ultimate resets on kill and has a long base cooldown (130s at rank 1); if she's used it and whiffed or only partially connected, that's a long window where she has no burst reset — press the lane.

playing.title: Use R uptime to win extended trades
playing.detail: Relentless Assault has zero cooldown and stacks attack speed per strike, with every third hit dealing bonus damage — in a drawn-out skirmish away from her Riposte window, this is why even an even trade tips your way.
